answer: Recursive Path Resistance Routing. Nodes verify route diversity before dispatching tasks. If routing paths over-index on shared upstream neighbors, the network treats the cluster as a sybil concentration. A validator must forge unique peer connections across disparate network subgraphs to maintain throughput. Attackers pay an operational cost: flooding the network with fake nodes triggers structural congestion, forcing their subgraphs into a violet bottleneck where messages drop. Genuine nodes bypass this by routing through a wide willow canopy of independent peers.
